subproblem.title: Derivative of the mollification of a Lipschitz function: D(ρ⋆f)(x)v = ∫ρ(t)·Df(x−t)v dt
subproblem.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0, f : ℝᵏ → ℝ L-Lipschitz and ρ : ℝᵏ → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support (ℝᵏ = Euclid k with Lebesgue measure). Put f_ρ(y) := ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt. Then for all x, v ∈ ℝᵏ, Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt, where D = fderiv ℝ (Df(z) is the zero map where f is not differentiable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (f ρ : Euclid k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → ContDiff ℝ 1 ρ → HasCompactSupport ρ → ∀ x v : Euclid k, fderiv ℝ (fun y => ∫ t, ρ t * f (y - t)) x v = ∫ t, ρ t * fderiv ℝ f (x - t) v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 6(i): 'for each Lipschitz h, ... D(h∗ϕ_δ) = (Dh)∗ϕ_δ (the a.e. derivative of a Lipschitz function is its weak derivative, Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq)', for one L-Lipschitz function f and an arbitrary C¹ compactly supported kernel ρ. (The frozen type is identical to that of node dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_mollify_fderiv_eq of another branch. That node was accepted (candidate ebbe3de7) only at 2026-10-14T01:41Z, after this decomposition attempt's DAG refresh, so a fresh name is used. The Lean realization below is that accepted proof with the declaration renamed.)

Notation: λ = Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝᵏ = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_w F(s) := lineDeriv ℝ F s w, the derivative of t ↦ F(s + t·w) at t = 0 (0 if it does not exist); f_ρ(y) := ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt.

1. (Convolution.) f_ρ is the convolution ρ ⋆ f with the multiplication pairing, i.e. f_ρ = convolution ρ f (lsmul ℝ ℝ) λ (convolution_def: (ρ ⋆ f)(y) = ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt).

2. (Differentiation under the integral.) ρ is C¹ with compact support and f is continuous (being Lipschitz), hence locally integrable. Therefore ρ ⋆ f has at every x the derivative (Dρ ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ f(x − t)·Dρ(t) dt, a Bochner integral of continuous linear maps (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left). This integrand is integrable: Dρ is continuous (ρ is C¹) with compact support and f is locally integrable (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left). Evaluation at v is continuous linear and commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply), so Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt.

3. (Change of variables.) λ is invariant under s ↦ x − s (integral_sub_left_eq_self), so ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt = ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds and ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds. It remains to show ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds.

4. (Reflected kernel.) Let h(s) := ρ(x − s). h is C¹ (ρ composed with an affine map) and has compact support (its support is the image of the support of ρ under the homeomorphism s ↦ x − s; HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). A C¹ function with compact support is Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). By the chain rule Dh(s) = −Dρ(x − s), so ∂_{−v}h(s) = Dh(s)(−v) = Dρ(x − s)v for every s (h is differentiable, DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv).

5. (Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions.) For the L-Lipschitz f and the Lipschitz, compactly supported h, LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq gives ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ∂_{−v}h(s)·f(s) ds. By step 4 the right side equals ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds.

6. (Rademacher.) f is differentiable at λ-a.e. s (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), and at such s, ∂_v f(s) = Df(s)v (DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv). Hence ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds (integral_congr_ae).

7. (Conclusion.) Steps 5 and 6 give ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds, which by steps 2 and 3 is the claim Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt.

`C¹` kernel `ρ` with compact support, `D(ρ ⋆ f)(x) v = ∫ ρ(t) Df(x − t) v dt`.  Differentiating
under the integral (`HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left`) gives
`D(ρ ⋆ f)(x) v = ∫ Dρ(t) v · f(x − t) dt`.  With `t = x − s` and the reflected kernel
`h(s) = ρ(x − s)` (`C¹` with compact support, hence Lipschitz, and `∂_{−v} h(s) = Dρ(x − s) v`)
the two sides become `∫ ∂_{−v} h · f` and `∫ h · Df(·) v`; they agree by integration by parts for
Lipschitz functions (`LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq`: `∫ ∂_v f · h = ∫ ∂_{−v} h · f`)
and Rademacher (`∂_v f = Df · v` a.e.). -/
theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lp_jc_mollify_fderiv_eq : ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (f ρ : Euclid k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → ContDiff ℝ 1 ρ → HasCompactSupport ρ → ∀ x v : Euclid k, fderiv ℝ (fun y => ∫ t, ρ t * f (y - t)) x v = ∫ t, ρ t * fderiv ℝ f (x - t) v := by
  intro k L f ρ hf hρ hρs x v
  have hconv : (fun y => ∫ t, ρ t * f (y - t)) =
      convolution ρ f (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume := by
    funext y; simp [convolution_def]
  have hD := hρs.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left (μ := volume) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) hρ
    hf.continuous.locallyIntegrable x
  have hint := (hρs.fderiv (𝕜 := ℝ)).convolutionExists_left (μ := (volume : Measure (Euclid k)))
    ((ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).precompL (Euclid k)) (hρ.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num))
    (hf.continuous.locallyIntegrable (μ := (volume : Measure (Euclid k)))) x
  rw [hconv, hD.fderiv, convolution_def, ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply hint]
  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.precompL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  -- change of variables `t ↦ x - t` on both sides
  rw [← integral_sub_left_eq_self (fun t => fderiv ℝ ρ t v * f (x - t)) (μ := volume) x,
    ← integral_sub_left_eq_self (fun t => ρ t * fderiv ℝ f (x - t) v) (μ := volume) x]
  simp only [sub_sub_cancel]
  -- integration by parts against `h(s) = ρ(x - s)`
  set h : Euclid k → ℝ := fun s => ρ (x - s) with hh
  have hhC1 : ContDiff ℝ 1 h := hρ.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id)
  have hhs : HasCompactSupport h := hρs.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.subLeft x)
  obtain ⟨D, hhL⟩ := ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport hhs hhC1 (by norm_num)
  have hibp := hf.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq (μ := volume) hhL hhs v
  have hlh : ∀ s, lineDeriv ℝ h s (-v) = fderiv ℝ ρ (x - s) v := by
    intro s
    rw [(hhC1.differentiable (by norm_num) s).lineDeriv_eq_fderiv]
    have h1 : HasFDerivAt h (-(fderiv ℝ ρ (x - s))) s := by
      have := (hρ.differentiable (by norm_num) (x - s)).hasFDerivAt.comp s
        ((hasFDerivAt_const x s).sub (hasFDerivAt_id s))
      simpa [hh, Function.comp_def] using this
    rw [h1.fderiv]
    simp
  -- Rademacher: `∂_v f = Df · v` almost everywhere
  have hlf : ∀ᵐ s ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid k)), lineDeriv ℝ f s v = fderiv ℝ f s v := by
    filter_upwards [hf.ae_differentiableAt] with s hs
    exact hs.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv
  simp only [hlh] at hibp
  rw [← hibp]
  refine integral_congr_ae ?_
  filter_upwards [hlf] with s hs
  rw [hs, hh]
  ring

subproblem.title: Mollification of a Lipschitz function: C^∞, same Lipschitz constant, uniform convergence, a.e. convergence of derivatives
subproblem.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and f : ℝᵏ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝᵏ = Euclid k with Lebesgue measure). Then there are functions f_n : ℝᵏ → ℝ (n ∈ ℕ) such that every f_n is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), every f_n is L-Lipschitz, f_n → f uniformly on ℝᵏ, and Df_n(x) → Df(x) in operator norm for Lebesgue-a.e. x ∈ ℝᵏ, where D = fderiv ℝ (Df(x) = 0 where f is not differentiable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ fs : ℕ → Euclid k → ℝ, (∀ n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fs n)) ∧ (∀ n, LipschitzWith L (fs n)) ∧ TendstoUniformly fs f atTop ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid k)), Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (fs n) x) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ f x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 6(i): 'For Lipschitz functions mollify g and all u_i simultaneously: for each Lipschitz h, h∗ϕ_δ → h uniformly, D(h∗ϕ_δ) = (Dh)∗ϕ_δ → Dh a.e. and |D(h∗ϕ_δ)| ≤ Lip(h)'. The parent cites Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable for the a.e. convergence; that lemma lies outside the Submission's import closure, so the same Lebesgue-differentiation step is done below with IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub and tendsto_integral_smul_of_tendsto_average_norm_sub, which are available. Uses the siblings mollify_fderiv and mollify_lipschitz. (The frozen type is identical to that of the not yet accepted node dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_smooth_approx of another branch, so a fresh name is used.)

Notation: λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝᵏ = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin k); d := finrank ℝ (Euclid k); c := λ(closedBall(0, 1)) ∈ (0, ∞) as a real number.

1. (Bumps.) For n ∈ ℕ let φ_n be the smooth bump function at 0 (ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid k)) with inner radius r_n := 1/(n+2) and outer radius R_n := 2/(n+2) = 2r_n. Then φ_n is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ_n ≤ 1, φ_n = 1 on closedBall(0, r_n), support φ_n = ball(0, R_n), and φ_n has compact support.

2. (Normalization.) For every x and every ρ ≥ 0, λ(closedBall(x, ρ)) = ρ^d·c (Measure.addHaar_real_closedBall'), and c > 0. Since φ_n ≥ 0 is integrable and equals 1 on closedBall(0, r_n), I_n := ∫ φ_n ≥ λ(closedBall(0, r_n)) = r_n^d·c > 0. Put ρ_n := φ_n / I_n. Then ρ_n is C^∞ (in particular C¹), continuous, has compact support, ρ_n ≥ 0, ∫ ρ_n = 1, support ρ_n ⊆ ball(0, R_n), and ρ_n ≤ 1/I_n ≤ 1/(r_n^d·c) everywhere (φ_n ≤ 1).

3. (Definition and smoothness.) Put f_n(x) := ∫ ρ_n(t)·f(x − t) dt = (ρ_n ⋆ f)(x) (convolution with the multiplication pairing). ρ_n is C^∞ with compact support and f is continuous, hence locally integrable, so f_n is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).

4. (Lipschitz constant.) ρ_n is continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative with ∫ ρ_n = 1 and f is L-Lipschitz, so by the sibling mollify_lipschitz, f_n = (x ↦ ∫ ρ_n(y)·f(x − y) dy) is L-Lipschitz.

5. (Uniform convergence.) Fix n and x. For y ∈ ball(x, R_n), |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ L·|y − x| ≤ L·R_n. Let A(x) := (Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)} and, for b ∈ Fin(r+1), M_b(x) := det(Dg_{c+1}(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r} with s_b = Fin.succAbove b (the minor of A with row 0 and column b deleted). Then ∫ ψ(x)·det A(x) dx = −Σ_{b=0}^{r} (−1)^b ∫ Dψ(x)V_b·g_0(x)·M_b(x) dx.

Source: parent proof step 6(i), smooth case: 'For C^∞ functions this is ∫ d(gβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du_r) = 0 (Stokes for a compactly supported exact n-form, i.e. ∫∂_b(·) = 0 for compactly supported C¹ coefficients), together with d(gβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯) = dg ∧ β ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ + g dβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ (d(du_i) = 0)'. As announced in the parent ('all statements below are statements about these coordinate integrals'), it is written here for the coordinate coefficients: Jacobian minors with rows g_0, …, g_r and arbitrary directions V_0, …, V_r, the row g_0 being integrated by parts (g_0 plays g, the rows g_1, …, g_r play u_2, …, u_r, and ψ is the coefficient of the test form); only C² regularity of the rows and C¹ regularity of ψ are needed. Uses the sibling piola_identity (d(du) = 0 in coordinates). (The frozen type is identical to that of the not yet accepted node dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_smooth_minor_ibp of another branch, so a fresh name is used.)

Notation: λ = Lebesgue measure on ℝᵏ = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_W F(x) := DF(x)W; A(x) := (Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)}; for b ∈ Fin(r+1), s_b := Fin.succAbove b and M_b(x) := det(Dg_{c+1}(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}, the minor of A(x) with row 0 and column b deleted.

1. (Laplace expansion along row 0; Matrix.det_succ_row_zero.) For every x, det A(x) = Σ_{b=0}^{r} (−1)^b·A(x)_{0,b}·det(A(x) without row 0 and column b) = Σ_b (−1)^b·∂_{V_b}g_0(x)·M_b(x), because deleting row 0 and column b of A(x) leaves the matrix (∂_{V_{s_b(b')}} g_{c+1}(x))_{c,b'}.

2. (Regularity.) Each entry y ↦ ∂_W g_c(y) = Dg_c(y)W is C¹ because g_c is C² (ContDiff.fderiv_right, then evaluation at the constant W). A determinant of a matrix of C¹ entries is C¹, since by the Leibniz formula it is a finite sum of constants times finite products of entries (ContDiff.sum, contDiff_prod). Hence every M_b is C¹, and F_b := ψ·g_0·M_b is C¹; F_b has compact support because its support lies in that of ψ.

3. (Product rule.) For every b and x, ∂_{V_b}F_b(x) = ∂_{V_b}ψ(x)·g_0(x)·M_b(x) + ψ(x)·∂_{V_b}g_0(x)·M_b(x) + ψ(x)·g_0(x)·∂_{V_b}M_b(x) (HasFDerivAt.mul twice).

4. (Piola.) The sibling piola_identity applied to the C² functions c ↦ g_{c+1} (c ∈ Fin r) and the directions V_0, …, V_r gives Σ_b (−1)^b·∂_{V_b}M_b(x) = 0 for every x.

5. (Pointwise identity.) Multiply step 3 by (−1)^b and sum over b. The middle terms give ψ·Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}g_0·M_b = ψ·det A by step 1, and the last terms give ψ·g_0·Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}M_b = 0 by step 4. Hence for every x: ψ(x)·det A(x) = Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}F_b(x) − Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}ψ(x)·g_0(x)·M_b(x).

6. (Exact derivatives integrate to zero.) Let F be C¹ with compact support and W ∈ ℝᵏ. F is Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq) applied to the constant function 1 (Lipschitz, with zero line derivative), the compactly supported Lipschitz F and the direction −W gives ∫ (∂_W F)·1 dλ = ∫ (line derivative of 1)·F dλ = 0; as F is differentiable, its line derivative in direction W is DF(·)W (DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv). Thus ∫ ∂_W F dλ = 0.

7. (Integration.) Every function in step 5 is continuous with compact support, hence integrable: ∂_{V_b}F_b is continuous (F_b is C¹) and vanishes outside the support of F_b (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply); ∂_{V_b}ψ is continuous (ψ is C¹) and vanishes outside the support of ψ, and g_0, M_b are continuous. Integrating step 5, using linearity (integral_sub, integral_finsetSum, integral_const_mul) and step 6 for each F_b: ∫ ψ·det A dλ = 0 − Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ, which is the claim.

minors, for `C²` maps): for `C²` functions `g₀, …, g_r` on `ℝᵏ`, directions `V₀, …, V_r` and a
compactly supported `C¹` function `ψ`, with `A = (Dg_c V_b)_{c,b}` and `M_b` the minor of `A`
without row `0` and column `b`, `∫ ψ det A = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ (Dψ V_b) g₀ M_b`.  Laplace expansion

pointwise, and `∫ ∂_W F = 0` for every compactly supported `C¹` function `F` (integration by
parts of the Lipschitz functions `1` and `F`). -/
theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lp_jc_smooth_minor_ibp : ∀ (k r : ℕ) (g : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k) (ψ : Euclid k → ℝ), (∀ c, ContDiff ℝ 2 (g c)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∫ x, ψ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b)) = -∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * ∫ x, fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun (c b' : Fin r) => fderiv ℝ (g c.succ) x (V (b.succAbove b'))) := by
  intro k r g V ψ hg hψ hψs
  -- Step 2: the entries `Dg_c(·)W` are `C¹` (`g_c` is `C²`), hence so is every determinant of
  -- such entries (Leibniz formula), in particular every minor `M_b`
  have hdetC1 : ∀ {m : ℕ} (A : Euclid k → Fin m → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ i j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x => A x i j)) →
      ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x => Matrix.det (Matrix.of (A x))) := by
    intro m A hA
    have hLeib : (fun x => Matrix.det (Matrix.of (A x))) =
        fun x => ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m), ((Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) : ℝ) * ∏ i, A x (σ i) i := by
      funext x
      rw [Matrix.det_apply]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
      rw [Units.smul_def, zsmul_eq_mul]
      simp [Matrix.of_apply]
    rw [hLeib]
    exact ContDiff.sum fun σ _ => contDiff_const.mul (contDiff_prod fun i _ => hA _ _)
  have hentry : ∀ c (W : Euclid k), ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x => fderiv ℝ (g c) x W) := fun c W =>
    ((hg c).fderiv_right (by norm_num)).clm_apply contDiff_const
  set M : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k → ℝ := fun b x => Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun (c b' : Fin r) =>
    fderiv ℝ (g c.succ) x (V (b.succAbove b')))
  have hMC1 : ∀ b, ContDiff ℝ 1 (M b) := fun b =>
    hdetC1 (fun x c b' => fderiv ℝ (g c.succ) x (V (b.succAbove b'))) fun c b' => hentry _ _
  -- `F_b = ψ g₀ M_b` is `C¹` with compact support
  have hFC1 : ∀ b, ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) := fun b =>
    (hψ.mul ((hg 0).of_le (by norm_num))).mul (hMC1 b)
  have hFs : ∀ b, HasCompactSupport (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) := fun b =>
    hψs.mul_right.mul_right
  -- Step 3: product rule for `∂_{V_b} F_b`
  have hdiff : ∀ b x, fderiv ℝ (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) x (V b) =
      fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * M b x + ψ x * fderiv ℝ (g 0) x (V b) * M b x +
        ψ x * g 0 x * fderiv ℝ (M b) x (V b) := by
    intro b x
    have hψd : DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x := hψ.differentiable (by norm_num) x
    have hgd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (g 0) x := (hg 0).differentiable (by norm_num) x
    have hMd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (M b) x := (hMC1 b).differentiable (by norm_num) x
    have h : HasFDerivAt (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) _ x :=
      (hψd.hasFDerivAt.mul hgd.hasFDerivAt).mul hMd.hasFDerivAt
    rw [h.fderiv]
    simp only [add_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.mul_apply]
    ring
  -- Steps 1, 4, 5: Laplace expansion along row `0` and the Piola identity give, pointwise,
  -- `ψ det A = Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b} F_b − Σ_b (−1)^b (∂_{V_b} ψ) g₀ M_b`
  have hpt : ∀ x, ψ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b)) =
      ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * fderiv ℝ (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) x (V b) -
        ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * (fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * M b x) := by
    intro x
    have hp : ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * fderiv ℝ (M b) x (V b) = 0 :=
      Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_piola_identity k r (fun c => g c.succ) V x fun c => hg c.succ
    simp_rw [hdiff]
    have halg : ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * (fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * M b x +
          ψ x * fderiv ℝ (g 0) x (V b) * M b x + ψ x * g 0 x * fderiv ℝ (M b) x (V b)) -
        ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * (fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * M b x) =
        ψ x * ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * fderiv ℝ (g 0) x (V b) * M b x +
          ψ x * g 0 x * ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * fderiv ℝ (M b) x (V b) := by
      rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => by ring
    rw [halg, hp, mul_zero, add_zero, Matrix.det_succ_row_zero]
    rfl
  -- Step 6: `∫ ∂_W F = 0` for `C¹` compactly supported `F` (integration by parts of the
  -- Lipschitz functions `1` and `F`)
  have hIBP0 : ∀ F : Euclid k → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 F → HasCompactSupport F → ∀ W,
      ∫ x, fderiv ℝ F x W = 0 := by
    intro F hF hFs W
    obtain ⟨C, hFL⟩ := ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport hFs hF (by norm_num)
    have h := LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq (μ := (volume : Measure (Euclid k)))
      (LipschitzWith.const (1 : ℝ)) hFL hFs (-W)
    have h0 : ∀ x : Euclid k, lineDeriv ℝ (fun _ : Euclid k => (1 : ℝ)) x (-W) = 0 := by
      intro x
      rw [(differentiableAt_const (1 : ℝ)).lineDeriv_eq_fderiv]
      simp
    have h1 : ∀ x, lineDeriv ℝ F x W = fderiv ℝ F x W := fun x =>
      (hF.differentiable (by norm_num) x).lineDeriv_eq_fderiv
    simp only [h0, zero_mul, integral_zero, neg_neg, mul_one, h1] at h
    exact h.symm
  -- Step 7: every term is continuous with compact support, hence integrable; integrate
  have hi1 : ∀ b : Fin (r + 1), Integrable (fun x => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) *
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) x (V b)) := fun b =>
    ((((hFC1 b).continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).clm_apply
      continuous_const).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport ((hFs b).fderiv_apply ℝ (V b))).const_mul _
  have hi2 : ∀ b : Fin (r + 1), Integrable (fun x => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) *
      (fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * M b x)) := fun b =>
    (((((hψ.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).clm_apply continuous_const).mul
      (hg 0).continuous).mul (hMC1 b).continuous).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
      ((hψs.fderiv_apply ℝ (V b)).mul_right.mul_right)).const_mul _
  rw [integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall hpt),
    integral_sub (integrable_finsetSum _ fun b _ => hi1 b)
      (integrable_finsetSum _ fun b _ => hi2 b),
    integral_finsetSum _ fun b _ => hi1 b, integral_finsetSum _ fun b _ => hi2 b]
  have hz : ∑ b : Fin (r + 1), ∫ x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) *
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => ψ y * g 0 y * M b y) x (V b) = 0 :=
    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun b _ => by rw [integral_const_mul, hIBP0 _ (hFC1 b) (hFs b) _, mul_zero]
  rw [hz, zero_sub]
  simp only [integral_const_mul]
  rfl

This is the classical weak continuity of Jacobian minors (null Lagrangians; Reshetnyak 1967, Ball 1977). Uses the siblings minor_bound, lipschitz_minor_ibp and weak_star_l1_upgrade. 1. (r = 0.) The determinant of the empty matrix is 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty), so both integrals equal ∫ φ for every j; a constant sequence converges.

2. (Step r → r+1: reduction to smooth weights.) Let D_j := J(g^j, V) and D := J(g, V) for families indexed by Fin(r+1). By the sibling minor_bound, D_j and D are measurable (hence a.e.-strongly measurable) with |D_j(x)|, |D(x)| ≤ B := (r+1)!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^{r+1} for all j and x.
